title: The buy-back step has no operation of its own and the consumed rows have no published operation names
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 Endpoints table; Ownership Map v1 API rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; API Specification v4
description: The legacy story names two endpoints, GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} and POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings. Neither opens a buy-back: the first is the asset read moved to the target base, the second is the pricing story's listing operation, and the inventory adds POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations, which is rwb-valuation's under ASM-A6-api-6. No source names an operation that opens a buy-back, and no source publishes the operation name or identifier of the rwb-deviation raise, of the rwb-decision approval child workflow or of the rwb-case case-move answer.
evidence: Legacy Endpoints: GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} (Asset and disposal R); POST /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId}/listings (Asset and disposal C). Ownership Map: POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations owner S8; GET /assets and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings owner S5; POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ASM-A6-api-6). Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: Decision: child: approval.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset with the owners of rwb-case and rwb-deviation
proposed: Declare the two asset reads as provided, the four consumed rows with the placeholder and a faked answer, and the buy-back as an element of the Asset answer rather than an operation; confirm each consumed name with its owner before the baseline is tagged.

title: Which table and column hold the buy-back terms and the template price is not settled and the template price has no field identifier
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1; Ownership Map v1 table rows; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-61; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23
description: The rules say the buy-back terms are agreed and completed at the template price, but no source gives the price a field identifier or names the table that holds it. listing carries start_price, floor_price and status (DF-SAL-004, DF-SAL-005, DF-SAL-008) and asset_sale carries contract_date, sale_date and sale_price (DF-SAL-012 to DF-SAL-014); the template itself is the template table, which the Ownership Map gives to P6 rwb-comms, and no TSD gives a read operation for it. Whether the template price sits on the listing, on the sale terms or in a third table is therefore unstated.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.1: listing DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008; asset_sale DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019. Ownership Map: template owner P6 (Architecture v5 slide 41, rwb-comms owns notices, templates, merge fields). Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24 Agree the buy-back terms at the template price; R-DIS-61 Complete the buy-back at the governed template price.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset with the owner of rwb-comms and the data steward
proposed: Write the terms on asset_sale with listing_id pointing at the buy-back listing and sale_price taken from the template price reference with its template version; add no table and no column and leave the price field and its read operation to P6.

title: The approval the limit requires has no limit value in any source and no published approval shape
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; Ownership Map v1 table rows
description: The legacy story, the FSD rule VR-S5-023-1 and R-DIS-24 all require the approval the limit requires, and none of them gives the limit or says who holds it. The ownership map gives approval to P7 rwb-decision and the delegated-authority table to P4 rwb-access, the approval is the kit's approval child workflow on rwb-decision, and neither its element names nor its answered and refused shapes are published in the sources read for this story.
evidence: Legacy AC1: with the approval the limit requires. FSD A2.23.3.1: VR-S5-023-1 Floor price below the approver's limit and MSG-S5-001 with the {pct} and {limit} placeholders. Ownership Map: approval owner P7; Architecture v5 slide 41 rwb-access owns the DoA table. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: Decision: child: approval.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-decision with the owner of rwb-access
proposed: Take the approval as the kit's approval child workflow on rwb-decision and read the limit from the delegated-authority rows of rwb-access at their version; write no limit value in code, in a test or in a fixture.

title: The buy-back channel and the buy-back listing status have no value in the closed lists
source: TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.2; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-032 Data
description: The buy-back is opened as a listing of the asset, and every listing row carries sale_channel and status, both closed lists. LOV-SALE-CHANNEL offers DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION and RAMC and LOV-LISTING offers DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN; neither carries a buy-back value and no source says which value an approved buy-back writes or whether the holding status of the asset moves.
evidence: TSD S5 T3.2: LOV-SALE-CHANNEL = DUTCH_AUCTION, BROKER, DIRECT, LED_AUCTION, RAMC; LOV-LISTING = DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, WITHDRAWN; LOV-HOLDING = HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, RENTED. TSD S5 T3.1 listing DF-SAL-003 sale_channel and DF-SAL-008 status are required.
owner_role: Owner of the reference data with the tech lead of rwb-asset
proposed: Read both lists as reference data at their version and carry the value as a placeholder until the reference-data owner publishes a buy-back entry; add no list value in code and leave the asset holding status unchanged in this step.

title: Legacy AC1 gives no from state while the buy-back rule starts at ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER and the asset is held
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-19, R-DIS-20, R-DIS-24; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T4
description: AC1 states only that the data and the rule version are in place, and it names no case state. The rule that agrees the buy-back terms, R-DIS-24, runs from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, which the disposal machine reaches from ASSET_HELD through R-DIS-19 and R-DIS-20, while the legacy criterion and the FSD describe the asset as held when the buy-back is opened. The state the step sees and the state the rule starts from are therefore described differently.
evidence: Legacy AC1: Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place. Business Rules v4: R-DIS-19 from ASSET_HELD to ROUTE_RECOMMENDED; R-DIS-20 from ROUTE_RECOMMENDED to ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER; R-DIS-24 from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER on ROUTE_APPROVED with route = buy_back and second_signature given to ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-decision with the owner of rwb-case
proposed: Read the case state and the route on the rwb-case contract, require ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER with the buy-back route for R-DIS-24, and let the case-move answer carry ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK; state in the tests that the asset is held while the route is with the approver.

title: The FSD lists the customer as an also-user of the feature and the rights matrix has no customer role
source: FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 A2.23.3.3; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20
description: The FSD gives the feature the sale officer as primary user and Head of NPA and Customer (borrower) as also-users. TSD S5 T6.1, which is the rights matrix of the module, has no customer or borrower role, and Architecture v5 slide 20 states that partners and customers do not use gateway-bff and reach the bank through the partner gateway to rwb-partner. The role the borrower acts under, and whether the former owner sees or signs the buy-back of the Workbench at all, is therefore not settled.
evidence: FSD A2.23.3.3: Sale officer, Primary; Head of NPA, Customer (borrower), Also uses. TSD S5 T6.1 lists 30 roles, none of them a customer or borrower. Architecture v5 slide 20: Partners do not use it: partner gateway to rwb-partner.
owner_role: Owner of rwb-access with the sales business owner
proposed: Represent the former owner by the sale officer acting on the case and carry the former owner as a party key the owner's contract answers; add no customer role, no customer screen and no external edge in this story.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: Split plan requirement rows for this key; Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S5-010; FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 requirements served
description: The plan row for this story carries an empty requirement list, while the program and the FSD give the slice REQ-S5-010, that a transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval. The trace therefore rests on the module requirement and not on a plan row.
evidence: Business Requirements Program v4: REQ-S5-010 A transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval, Must, Head of NPA, E4. FSD S5 requirements served repeats the same row. The plan requirement list for RWB-S5-E4032-APP and RWB-S5-E4032-CON is empty.
owner_role: Traceability manager with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both stories to REQ-S5-010 in place of a plan requirement row and let the register carry the absence.

title: No published surface exists for the buy-back step so the baseline declares it as an element and the consumed rows as placeholders
source: Legacy RWB-E4-032 Endpoints table; Ownership Map v1 API rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T-A.1 and T3.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41
description: The contract baseline has to declare the buy-back surface, and no source gives one: there is no operation that opens a buy-back, no operation name for the rwb-case case-move answer, the rwb-deviation raise or the rwb-decision approval, and no value in LOV-SALE-CHANNEL or LOV-LISTING for a buy-back. The only operations the sources give the service are the two asset reads, the listing and the auction rounds, and the valuations that belong to rwb-valuation under ASM-A6-api-6.
evidence: Ownership Map: GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds owner S5; POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 (ASM-A6-api-6); POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations owner S8. TSD S5 T-A.1 lists API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 only. TSD S5 T3.2 lists LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING without a buy-back value.
proposed: Declare the two asset reads as provided, the buy-back as an element of the Asset answer and as rows of listing and asset_sale, and the four consumed rows with the placeholder; add no operation, no list value and no property of another owner.

title: The approval answer and the template price element are not published and their fakes are derived
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 OUT; Ownership Map v1 table rows; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-24
description: The baseline must fake the approval answer and the template price read, and no source publishes either shape: the approval is named only as the child approval of the kit on rwb-decision, and the template price has neither a field identifier nor a read operation, while the template table belongs to P6 rwb-comms and not to rwb-document. The fake answers are therefore derived from the owner documents and carry the placeholder.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: Decision: child: approval. Ownership Map: approval owner P7; template owner P6. TSD S5 T3.1 has no template price column and no field identifier for one. Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24: Agree the buy-back terms at the template price.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset with the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-comms
proposed: Derive the approval and template fakes from the owners' published documents, mark the fields the source does not give with the placeholder and hold them under the drift test.

title: The asset row is absent from the Ownership Map table list although three sources give it to S5
source: Ownership Map v1 table rows; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 T3.1
description: The buy-back step reads the asset row it opens the listing against, and the Ownership Map has no row for the asset table: it lists listing and asset_sale as S5's only. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-asset assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings and auction rounds and slide 19 gives the schema rwb_asset, and TSD S5 T3.1 defines the asset object, so the owner is read as S5 without a map row and the reading is recorded rather than assumed.
evidence: Ownership Map: listing owner S5, asset_sale owner S5, no asset row. Architecture v5 slide 41: S5 rwb-asset owns assets taken on, holding, floor price, listings, auction rounds. Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT: DB writes schema rwb_asset. TSD S5 T3.1: asset (EXTEND ACE Asset) with DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042.
owner_role: Solution architect with the data steward
proposed: Read the asset row as S5's from Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1, record the map omission, and add the row to the Ownership Map in its next version.
